# Shared dispatcher. Never capture or wrap an unknown user function.
if (( ${+aliases[codex]} )); then
  print -u2 'iterm2-utils: codex alias conflict'
  return 1
fi
if (( ${+functions[codex]} )) && [[ ${functions[codex]} == ${_codex_restore_installed_body-} ]]; then
  return 0
fi
if (( ${+functions[codex]} )) && [[ ${functions[codex]} != *'iterm2-utils dispatcher'* ]]; then
  print -u2 'iterm2-utils: codex function conflict'
  return 1
fi
# REPLY is local to the caller. Unknown options are deliberately passed through.
function _iterm2_utils_classify {
  emulate -L zsh
  local arg command_name='' literal=0 need_value=0
  REPLY=interactive
  for arg in "$@"; do
    if (( need_value )); then
      need_value=0
      continue
    fi
    (( literal )) && continue
    case $arg in
      --) literal=1; continue ;;
      --help|-h|--version|-V)
        REPLY=passthrough; continue ;;
      --remote)
        REPLY=passthrough; need_value=1; continue ;;
      --remote=*|--remote-control|--ephemeral)
        REPLY=passthrough; continue ;;
      -c|--config|-m|--model|-C|--cd|-i|--image|-p|--profile|-s|--sandbox|-a|--ask-for-approval|--enable|--disable|--add-dir|--local-provider)
        need_value=1; continue ;;
      --no-daemon) continue ;;
      --config=*|--model=*|--cd=*|--image=*|--profile=*|--sandbox=*|--ask-for-approval=*|--enable=*|--disable=*|--add-dir=*|--local-provider=*|--oss|--full-auto|--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox|--no-alt-screen|--search)
        continue ;;
      --all|--last)
        [[ $command_name == resume || $command_name == fork ]] || REPLY=passthrough
        continue ;;
      --restore)
        if [[ $command_name == resume ]]; then
          REPLY=invalid-restore
          return
        fi
        REPLY=passthrough; continue ;;
      -*) REPLY=passthrough; continue ;;
    esac
    if [[ -z $command_name ]]; then
      case $arg in
        exec|e|review|agents|remote-control|app-server|login|logout|mcp|mcp-server|app|completion|sandbox|debug|apply|a|cloud|features|help)
          REPLY=passthrough; command_name=service ;;
        resume|fork) command_name=$arg ;;
        *) command_name=prompt ;;
      esac
    fi
  done
  (( need_value )) && REPLY=passthrough
  return 0
}


function codex() {
  : 'iterm2-utils dispatcher'
  local arg REPLY
  _iterm2_utils_classify "$@"
  if [[ $REPLY != interactive ]]; then
    command codex "$@"
    return $?
  fi
  if [[ ${ITERM2_UTILS_CODEX_NO_DAEMON:-0} == 1 ]]; then
    for arg in "$@"; do
      if [[ $arg == --no-daemon ]]; then
        command codex "$@"
        return $?
      fi
    done
    command codex --no-daemon "$@"
  else
    command codex "$@"
  fi
}

# Source after any existing codex function (for example codex-iterm2-status).
# Keep a copy of the installed body: a full .zshrc source may redefine codex first.
if (( ${+aliases[codex]} )); then
  print -u2 -- 'Codex: alias codex мешает функции восстановления; уберите alias и подключите файл снова'
  return 1
fi
if (( ${+functions[codex]} )) && [[ ${functions[codex]} != ${_codex_restore_installed_body-} ]]; then
  functions -c codex _codex_restore_previous
fi
typeset -g _codex_restore_root=${${(%):-%x}:A:h}

# Package installs pass the same verified absolute Python as the hook runtime.
# Standalone source usage retains its original executable entrypoint.
function _codex_restore_sessions {
  if [[ -n ${ITERM2_UTILS_PYTHON-} ]]; then
    "$ITERM2_UTILS_PYTHON" "$_codex_restore_root/codex-sessions" "$@"
  else
    "$_codex_restore_root/codex-sessions" "$@"
  fi
}

function _codex_restore_previous_call {
  if (( ${+functions[_codex_restore_previous]} )); then
    _codex_restore_previous "$@"
  else
    command codex "$@"
  fi
}

# REPLY is local to the caller. Unknown options are deliberately passed through.
function _codex_restore_classify {

function _codex_restore_call {
  emulate -L zsh
  local REPLY token='' result=0 _codex_restore_seen_no_daemon=0
  _codex_restore_classify "$@"
  if [[ $REPLY == invalid-restore ]]; then
    print -u2 -- 'Codex: используйте ровно codex resume --restore (без дополнительных аргументов)'
    return 2
  fi
  if [[ $REPLY != interactive ]]; then
    _codex_restore_previous_call "$@"
    return $?
  fi
  # A failed new registration must not lend the child a previous owner's token.
  local -x CODEX_RESTORE_TOKEN=''
  if [[ -z ${_codex_restore_no_daemon+x} ]]; then
    typeset -g _codex_restore_no_daemon=0
    [[ $(command codex --help 2>/dev/null) == *--no-daemon* ]] && _codex_restore_no_daemon=1
  fi
  if (( ! _codex_restore_no_daemon )); then
    _codex_restore_previous_call "$@"
    return $?
  fi
  local -a arguments=("$@") register_args
  (( _codex_restore_seen_no_daemon )) || arguments=(--no-daemon "${arguments[@]}")
  if [[ -n ${ITERM_SESSION_ID-} && ${TERM_PROGRAM-} == iTerm.app ]] && zmodload zsh/system 2>/dev/null; then
    # $$ remains the parent's PID inside ( ... ). Read the actual owner before
    # command substitution creates its own process; never fall back to $$.
    local shell_pid=$sysparams[pid]
    register_args=(register --terminal "$ITERM_SESSION_ID" --shell-pid "$shell_pid")
    [[ -n ${CODEX_RESTORE_REQUEST-} ]] && register_args+=(--request "$CODEX_RESTORE_REQUEST")
    token=$(_codex_restore_sessions "${register_args[@]}") || token=''
  fi
  if [[ -z $token ]]; then
    _codex_restore_previous_call "${arguments[@]}"
    return $?
  fi
  CODEX_RESTORE_TOKEN=$token
  {
    _codex_restore_previous_call "${arguments[@]}"
    result=$?
  } always {
    _codex_restore_sessions finish "$token" || true
  }
  return $result
}

function _codex_restore_select {
  emulate -L zsh
  local rows selected output result
  local -a fields
  rows=$(_codex_restore_sessions restore-list "$@") || return $?
  if [[ -z $rows ]]; then
    [[ ${1-} == --auto ]] || print -- 'Codex: восстанавливать нечего'
    return 0
  fi
  if (( ! ${+commands[fzf]} )); then
    print -u2 -- 'Codex: для выбора вкладок нужен fzf 0.60+'
    return 127
  fi
  selected=$(print -r -- "$rows" | command fzf --multi --bind=load:select-all --no-sort \
    --delimiter=$'\t' --with-nth=3.. --accept-nth=2 --prompt='Codex: ')
  result=$?
  if (( result == 130 || result == 1 )); then
    return 0
  elif (( result )); then
    print -u2 -- 'Codex: ошибка выбора fzf'
    return $result
  fi
  [[ -n $selected ]] || return 0
  # zsh preserves NUL bytes in command substitution. Capture the producer's
  # status before splitting; a read loop/process substitution would hide it.
  output=$(print -r -- "$selected" | _codex_restore_sessions restore-open) || return $?
  [[ -n $output ]] || return 0
  fields=("${(@0)output}")
  local uuid_pattern='^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$'
  if (( ${#fields} != 6 )) || [[ -n $fields[6] || ! $fields[1] =~ $uuid_pattern || ! $fields[2] =~ $uuid_pattern || $fields[3] != /* || $fields[4] != /* || $fields[5] != /* ]]; then
    print -u2 -- 'Codex: некорректный ответ restore-open'
    return 1
  fi
  if ! builtin cd -- "$fields[3]"; then
    _codex_restore_sessions restore-cancel "$fields[1]" || true
    return 1
  fi
  local -x CODEX_HOME=$fields[4] CODEX_RESTORE_REQUEST=$fields[1] CODEX_RESTORE_CACHE_DIR=$fields[5]
  codex resume "$fields[2]"
}

function _codex_restore_precmd {
  emulate -L zsh
  precmd_functions=(${precmd_functions:#_codex_restore_precmd})
  [[ ${_codex_restore_auto_ran-0} == 1 ]] && return 0
  typeset -g _codex_restore_auto_ran=1
  _codex_restore_select --auto
  # A failed picker must not stop the remaining precmd hooks (including cr).
  return 0
}

if [[ -o interactive && ${TERM_PROGRAM-} == iTerm.app && ${CODEX_RESTORE_NO_AUTO-0} != 1 && ${_codex_restore_auto_ran-0} != 1 ]]; then
  typeset -ga precmd_functions
  (( ${precmd_functions[(Ie)_codex_restore_precmd]} )) || precmd_functions+=(_codex_restore_precmd)
fi

function codex {
  if (( $# == 2 )) && [[ $1 == resume && $2 == --restore ]]; then
    _codex_restore_select
  else
    _codex_restore_call "$@"
  fi
}
typeset -g _codex_restore_installed_body=$functions[codex]

"""Resolve the installation even when invoked through a symlink from another cwd."""

"""Independent, metadata-only Codex session restoration components."""

"""Command boundary; lifecycle hooks always return the observational response."""
import argparse
from contextlib import contextmanager
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import sys
import time
from typing import Iterator

from . import registry, restore, snapshots, store, transcripts
from .iterm import ITerm
from .models import Paths


def _paths() -> Paths:
    return store.paths(Path(os.environ.get("CODEX_HOME", "~/.codex")),
                       Path(os.environ.get("CODEX_RESTORE_CACHE_DIR", "~/.cache/codex-resume")))


@contextmanager
def _deadline(seconds: float) -> Iterator[float]:
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    previous_handler = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGALRM)
    previous_timer = signal.getitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL)
    def expired(signum, frame):
        raise TimeoutError("hook deadline exceeded")
    signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, expired)
    signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, seconds)
    try:
        yield deadline
    finally:
        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, previous_handler)
        if previous_timer[0] > 0:
            remaining = max(0.000001, previous_timer[0] - seconds + max(0, deadline - time.monotonic()))
            signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, remaining, previous_timer[1])


def _hook() -> int:
    try:
        with _deadline(2.0) as deadline:
            event = json.load(sys.stdin)
            if not isinstance(event, dict) or event.get("hook_event_name") not in ("SessionStart", "UserPromptSubmit", "Stop"):
                return 0
            token = os.environ.get("CODEX_RESTORE_TOKEN", "")
            terminal = registry.normalize_terminal(os.environ.get("ITERM_SESSION_ID", ""))
            paths, client = _paths(), ITerm()
            client.deadline = deadline
            now = time.time()
            if registry.accept_event(paths, token, terminal, event, client.identity, now):
                snapshots.capture(paths, client, now, required_terminal=terminal, required_token=token)
    except Exception:
        pass
    finally:
        print("{}")
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    # Hook dispatch precedes parser and all setup, so even broken state is harmless.
    if argv == ["hook"]:
        return _hook()
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="codex-sessions")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    register = commands.add_parser("register")
    register.add_argument("--terminal", required=True)
    register.add_argument("--shell-pid", required=True, type=int)
    register.add_argument("--request")
    finish = commands.add_parser("finish")
    finish.add_argument("token")
    listing = commands.add_parser("restore-list")
    listing.add_argument("--auto", action="store_true")
    commands.add_parser("restore-open")
    cancel = commands.add_parser("restore-cancel")
    cancel.add_argument("request")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        paths = _paths()
        if args.command == "register":
            client = ITerm()
            started = client.identity(args.shell_pid)
            if not started:
                raise ValueError("cannot identify the calling shell")
            request = transcripts.normalize_uuid(args.request) if args.request is not None else None
            registration = registry.register(paths, args.terminal, args.shell_pid, started,
                                             client.launch_id(), time.time(), request)
            print(registration.token)
        elif args.command == "finish":
            registry.finish(paths, args.token)
        elif args.command == "restore-list":
            choices, notes = restore.choices(paths, ITerm(), args.auto, time.time())
            for note in notes:
                print(note, file=sys.stderr)
            for row in restore.rows(choices):
                print(row)
        elif args.command == "restore-open":
            selected = [line.rstrip("\n") for line in sys.stdin if line.rstrip("\n")]
            first = restore.prepare(paths, ITerm(), selected, os.environ.get("ITERM_SESSION_ID", ""), time.time())
            if first is not None:
                fields = (first.request, first.session.session_id, str(first.session.cwd),
                          str(first.session.codex_home), str(paths.state_dir.parent))
                sys.stdout.write("\0".join(fields) + "\0")
        elif args.command == "restore-cancel":
            restore.cancel(paths, args.request)
        return 0
    except Exception as exc:
        print("codex-sessions: %s" % exc, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

"""Bounded metadata-only bridge to the bundled source registry."""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import time
from .codexlib import registry, snapshots, store
from .codexlib.iterm import ITerm


def handle(event, settings, runner, metadata=None):
    if not metadata or event.name not in {'SessionStart','UserPromptSubmit','Stop'}:
        return
    home=Path(os.environ.get('CODEX_HOME',settings['restore_codex_home']))
    paths=store.paths(home,Path(os.environ.get('CODEX_RESTORE_CACHE_DIR',settings['restore_cache'])))
    client=ITerm(settings['it2'])
    client.process=settings['restore_process']
    # Preserve the dispatcher's OS-level deadline. Source registry lock waits and
    # subprocess calls remain bounded, and BaseException escapes to hook.main.
    client.deadline=time.monotonic()+2.0
    now=time.time()
    if registry.accept_event(paths,os.environ.get('CODEX_RESTORE_TOKEN',''),event.terminal_uuid,metadata,client.identity,now):
        snapshots.capture(paths,client,now,required_terminal=event.terminal_uuid,required_token=os.environ.get('CODEX_RESTORE_TOKEN',''))

"""Normalize an event in memory. No transcript reads or raw event persistence."""
from dataclasses import dataclass
import re
import hashlib
import json
try:
    from vendor.codex_status.status import EVENTS, terminal_id
except ImportError:
    from .vendor.codex_status.status import EVENTS, terminal_id

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Event:
    agent: str
    name: str
    session_id: str
    terminal_uuid: str
    turn_key: str | None
    tool_name: str | None
    notification_type: str | None
    background_running: bool
    tool_key: str | None = None
    source: str | None = None
    agent_id: str | None = None
    stop_hook_active: bool = False
    notification_key: str | None = None


def identifier(value):
    return value if isinstance(value,str) and re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,200}',value) else None


def normalize(raw: dict, agent: str, terminal_env: str | None) -> Event | None:
    if not isinstance(raw,dict) or agent not in {'codex','claude'}:
        return None
    terminal=terminal_id(terminal_env or '')
    supplied=raw.get('terminal_uuid')
    if not terminal or (supplied is not None and terminal_id(str(supplied)) != terminal):
        return None
    sid=identifier(raw.get('session_id'))
    name=raw.get('hook_event_name')
    if not sid or name not in (*EVENTS,'Notification','StopFailure','PostToolUseFailure'):
        return None
    source=raw.get('source')
    if source not in {'startup','resume','clear','compact'}:
        source=None
    # Preserve upstream pairing when permission events omit tool IDs; raw payload
    # exists only in this stack frame. Command-only canonicalization intentionally
    # ignores the permission-only description field.
    tool=raw.get('tool_name'); payload=raw.get('tool_input')
    if tool in {'Bash','apply_patch','Edit','Write'} and isinstance(payload,dict) and 'command' in payload:
        payload={'command':payload['command']}
    digest=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps([tool,payload],sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
    # Notification schema has message/title/type but no per-request ID. Keep
    # only its opaque identity, never presentation strings, beyond this frame.
    notification_key=None
    if agent=='claude' and name=='Notification':
        values=[raw.get(key) if isinstance(raw.get(key),str) else '' for key in ('notification_type','title','message')]
        notification_key=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(values).encode()).hexdigest()
    # Official SDK: the list contains in-flight work, irrespective of its free
    # status string. Unknown nonempty shapes conservatively suppress completion.
    return Event(agent,name,sid,terminal,identifier(raw.get('prompt_id') if agent == 'claude' else raw.get('turn_id')),identifier(raw.get('tool_name')),

"""Explicit-session it2 command construction; adapted from iterm2-status (MIT)."""
from .status import COLORS, terminal_id

def status_command(it2, terminal, state):
    terminal = terminal_id(terminal)
    if not terminal:
        return None
    color = COLORS[state['status']]
    return [str(it2), 'session', 'set-status', '--session', terminal,
            '--status', state['status'], '--dot-color', color,
            '--text-color', color, '--detail', state['detail'],
            '--background-tasks', str(len(state['agents']))]

if [[ -o interactive ]]; then
  # Don't run in IDE terminals. TERM_PROGRAM is set by the local terminal but not
  # forwarded over SSH. LC_TERMINAL is set by iTerm2 and may be forwarded over SSH.
  if [ \( -z "${TERM_PROGRAM-}" -o "${TERM_PROGRAM-}" = "iTerm.app" -o "${LC_TERMINAL-}" = "iTerm2" \) -a "${ITERM_ENABLE_SHELL_INTEGRATION_WITH_TMUX-}""$TERM" != "tmux-256color" -a "${ITERM_ENABLE_SHELL_INTEGRATION_WITH_TMUX-}""$TERM" != "screen" -a "${ITERM_SHELL_INTEGRATION_INSTALLED-}" = "" -a "$TERM" != linux -a "$TERM" != dumb ]; then
    ITERM_SHELL_INTEGRATION_INSTALLED=Yes
    ITERM2_SHOULD_DECORATE_PROMPT="1"

    # OSC 133 aid: per-command identifier the receiver uses to target a
    # specific mark for D-by-aid (and cascade-close when an outer command
    # like ssh dies before its inner remote shell's D arrives). The salt
    # is rolled once at shell-source time; the counter increments per
    # prompt cycle in iterm2_precmd.
    typeset -g ITERM2_AID_SALT="${RANDOM}${RANDOM}"
    typeset -gi ITERM2_AID_COUNTER=0
    # Pre-seeded so emissions before the first iterm2_precmd (e.g.
    # iterm2_print_state_data at install time) have a defined aid value
    # rather than the empty string.
    typeset -g ITERM2_CURRENT_AID="${ITERM2_AID_SALT}-0"

    # Indicates start of command output. Runs just before command executes.
    iterm2_before_cmd_executes() {
      if [ "$TERM_PROGRAM" = "iTerm.app" ]; then
        printf "\033]133;C;aid=%s\r\007" "$ITERM2_CURRENT_AID"
      else
        printf "\033]133;C;aid=%s\007" "$ITERM2_CURRENT_AID"
      fi
    }

    iterm2_set_user_var() {
      printf "\033]1337;SetUserVar=%s=%s\007" "$1" $(printf "%s" "$2" | base64 | tr -d '\n')
    }

    # Users can write their own version of this method. It should call
    # iterm2_set_user_var but not produce any other output.
    # e.g., iterm2_set_user_var currentDirectory $PWD
    # Accessible in iTerm2 (in a badge now, elsewhere in the future) as
    # \(user.currentDirectory).
    whence -v iterm2_print_user_vars > /dev/null 2>&1
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
      iterm2_print_user_vars() {
          true
      }
    fi

    # separator. nomultibyte + LC_ALL=C force byte-wise iteration so each UTF-8 byte
    # is encoded individually (matching how the receiver decodes it). Stores the
    # result in the global _iterm2_encoded_path rather than printing it, so the
    # caller reads a variable instead of forking a command substitution per prompt.
    iterm2_encode_path() {
      emulate -L zsh
      setopt nomultibyte
      local _iterm2_path="$1"
      local _iterm2_i _iterm2_ch _iterm2_hexch _iterm2_out=""
      local LC_ALL=C
      for (( _iterm2_i = 1; _iterm2_i <= ${#_iterm2_path}; ++_iterm2_i )); do
        _iterm2_ch="${_iterm2_path[_iterm2_i]}"
        if [[ "$_iterm2_ch" == [/._~A-Za-z0-9-] ]]; then
          _iterm2_out+="$_iterm2_ch"
        else
          printf -v _iterm2_hexch '%02X' "$(( #_iterm2_ch & 0xFF ))"
          _iterm2_out+="%$_iterm2_hexch"
        fi
      done
      _iterm2_encoded_path="$_iterm2_out"
    }

    iterm2_print_state_data() {
      local _iterm2_hostname="${iterm2_hostname-}"
      if [ -z "${iterm2_hostname:-}" ]; then
        _iterm2_hostname=$(hostname -f 2>/dev/null)
      fi
      # Sanitize the authority: a username or hostname with a URL-structural
      # character (/, ?, #, or whitespace) would silently restructure the URL -
      # recording the wrong directory, or (since the machineID query still parses)
      # poisoning localhost detection with a truncated host. Keep only a safe set so
      # a malformed label degrades to a clean name. The username keeps @ (an AD
      # login like alice@corp.com survives, since URL parsers split on the LAST @).
      local _iterm2_user="${USER//[^A-Za-z0-9._@-]/}"
      _iterm2_hostname="${_iterm2_hostname//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/}"

      # URL. This supersedes the older 1337;RemoteHost and 1337;CurrentDir codes.
      local _iterm2_encoded_path=""
      iterm2_encode_path "$PWD"

      local _iterm2_url="file://${_iterm2_user}@${_iterm2_hostname}${_iterm2_encoded_path}?machineID=${_iterm2_machine_id}"

    # Uses the OLD aid (the one in effect for the just-finished command). The
    # counter increments AFTER this call so the new A/B/C cycle starts fresh.
    iterm2_after_cmd_executes() {
      printf "\033]133;D;%s;aid=%s\007" "$STATUS" "$ITERM2_CURRENT_AID"
      iterm2_print_state_data

    iterm2_prompt_mark() {
      printf "\033]133;A;aid=%s\007" "$ITERM2_CURRENT_AID"

    # that records the PS2 prefix cells as an excluded subrange on the active
    # primary mark, so selection / share / AI consumers can subtract them.
    iterm2_ps2_mark() {
      printf "\033]133;A;k=s;aid=%s\007" "$ITERM2_CURRENT_AID"

      printf "\033]133;B;aid=%s\007" "$ITERM2_CURRENT_AID"

    #
    # 1) A command is entered at the prompt and you press return.
    #    The following steps happen:
    #    * iterm2_preexec is invoked
    #      * PS1 is set to ITERM2_PRECMD_PS1
    #      * ITERM2_SHOULD_DECORATE_PROMPT is set to 1
    #    * The command executes (possibly reading or modifying PS1)
    #    * iterm2_precmd is invoked
    #      * ITERM2_PRECMD_PS1 is set to PS1 (as modified by command execution)
    #      * PS1 gets our escape sequences added to it
    #    * zsh displays your prompt
    #    * You start entering a command
    #
    # 2) You press ^C while entering a command at the prompt.
    #    The following steps happen:
    #    * (iterm2_preexec is NOT invoked)
    #    * iterm2_precmd is invoked
    #      * iterm2_before_cmd_executes is called since we detected that iterm2_preexec was not run
    #      * (ITERM2_PRECMD_PS1 and PS1 are not messed with, since PS1 already has our escape
    #        sequences and ITERM2_PRECMD_PS1 already has PS1's original value)
    #    * zsh displays your prompt
    #    * You start entering a command

    # 3) A new shell is born.
    #    * PS1 has some initial value, either zsh's default or a value set before this script is sourced.
    #    * iterm2_precmd is invoked
    #      * ITERM2_SHOULD_DECORATE_PROMPT is initialized to 1
    #      * ITERM2_PRECMD_PS1 is set to the initial value of PS1
    #      * PS1 gets our escape sequences added to it
    #    * Your prompt is shown and you may begin entering a command.
    #
    # Invariants:
    # * ITERM2_SHOULD_DECORATE_PROMPT is 1 during and just after command execution, and "" while the prompt is
    #   shown and until you enter a command and press return.
    # * PS1 does not have our escape sequences during command execution
    # * After the command executes but before a new one begins, PS1 has escape sequences and
    #   ITERM2_PRECMD_PS1 has PS1's original value.
    iterm2_decorate_prompt() {
      # This should be a raw PS1 without iTerm2's stuff. It could be changed during command
      # execution.
      ITERM2_PRECMD_PS1="$PS1"
      ITERM2_PRECMD_PS2="$PS2"
      ITERM2_SHOULD_DECORATE_PROMPT=""

      # Add our escape sequences just before the prompt is shown.
      # Use ITERM2_SQUELCH_MARK for people who can't modify PS1 directly, like powerlevel9k users.
      # This is gross but I had a heck of a time writing a correct if statetment for zsh 5.0.2.
      local PREFIX=""
      if [[ $PS1 == *"$(iterm2_prompt_mark)"* ]]; then
        PREFIX=""
      elif [[ "${ITERM2_SQUELCH_MARK-}" != "" ]]; then
        PREFIX=""
      else
        PREFIX="%{$(iterm2_prompt_mark)%}"
      fi

      ITERM2_DECORATED_PS1="$PS1"

      # the typed-command region and so paste-helpers can advance past PS2 lines.
      # Skip if PS2 already contains our mark (user re-sourced this script) or if
      # the user has opted out via ITERM2_SQUELCH_PS2_MARK. The wrap is idempotent
      # in steady state because iterm2_preexec restores PS2 from
      # ITERM2_PRECMD_PS2 before the next cycle.
      if [[ $PS2 != *"$(iterm2_ps2_mark)"* ]] && [[ "${ITERM2_SQUELCH_PS2_MARK-}" == "" ]]; then
        PS2="%{$(iterm2_ps2_mark)%}$PS2%{$(iterm2_prompt_end)%}"
      fi
      ITERM2_DECORATED_PS2="$PS2"

    iterm2_precmd() {

        iterm2_before_cmd_executes

      # and BEFORE the new prompt is decorated. PS1's iterm2_prompt_mark
      # gets evaluated each time the prompt is drawn (it's inside %{ %}),
      # so the next A read will pick up the new value.
      ITERM2_AID_COUNTER=$((ITERM2_AID_COUNTER + 1))
      ITERM2_CURRENT_AID="${ITERM2_AID_SALT}-${ITERM2_AID_COUNTER}"

        iterm2_decorate_prompt
      fi
    }

    # This is not run if you press ^C while entering a command.
    iterm2_preexec() {

      PS1="$ITERM2_PRECMD_PS1"
      PS2="$ITERM2_PRECMD_PS2"
      ITERM2_SHOULD_DECORATE_PROMPT="1"
      iterm2_before_cmd_executes

    # sourcing this script. We know it is fast on macOS so we don't cache
    # it. That lets us handle the hostname changing like when you attach
    # to a VPN.
    if [ -z "${iterm2_hostname-}" ]; then

        iterm2_hostname=`hostname -f 2>/dev/null`
        # Some flavors of BSD (i.e. NetBSD and OpenBSD) don't have the -f option.
        if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
          iterm2_hostname=`hostname`
        fi
      fi
    fi

    # NON-EXPORTED shell variable (never `export`/`typeset -x`, so it cannot cross
    # ssh) as "1:<hmac>". We HMAC kern.bootsessionuuid with a fixed protocol key
    # rather than sending the raw per-boot UUID; iTerm2 HMACs its own the same way
    # and compares. The sysctl and openssl run once here, not per prompt. A known
    # non-Darwin host can't be this Mac, so it sends the empty value ("1:"); a Darwin
    # failure, or an OS we cannot determine at all (empty $OSTYPE), sends "0:"
    # (identity unavailable, so the receiver falls back to hostname matching).
    if [ -z "${_iterm2_machine_id+set}" ]; then
      case "${OSTYPE-}" in
        darwin*)
